title: Shortcuts to adiabaticity in five-level systems using counter-diabatic driving and time-rescaling optimization
authors: Jiahui Zhang, Wenyuan Wang, Fuquan Dou
abstract: Shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA) is a common protocol to realize high-fidelity and robust quantum control in various quantum systems. To date, STA has been widely applied in two- and three-level systems, whereas designing feasible strategies to achieve perfect quantum state engineering in multi-level systems still remains a challenging task. Here, we propose to use counterdiabatic (CD) driving and time-rescaling (TR) methods to construct multi-state stimulated Raman shortcut-to-adiabatic passage protocols for realizing robust and fast population transfer in chainwise-connected five-state systems. The first protocol is implemented by initially reducing the original five-state system to an equivalent two-state counterpart, and then designing the corresponding driving field by combining CD driving and unitary transformation. Further, we introduce the TR method to optimize the first protocol and thus offers an alternative solution. Numerical calculations show that both protocols can achieve complete population transfer and effectively suppress transient populations of all intermediate states. Compared with the first protocol, the optimized second exhibits better performance within a shorter evolution time.
summary: The paper addresses the challenge of controlling population transfer in complex five-level quantum systems by applying advanced Shortcuts to Adiabaticity protocols. It introduces a novel, optimized time-rescaling method ($	ext{M-STIRSAP-opt}$) that significantly improves speed and robustness compared to existing methods. This work provides a powerful theoretical framework for realizing fast, high-fidelity quantum state engineering in multi-level atomic or molecular systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing fast and robust quantum control protocols for achieving high-fidelity population transfer in complex multi-level quantum systems, specifically five-level chains.
main_result: The optimized time-rescaling protocol ($	ext{M-STIRSAP-opt}$) was shown to achieve complete population transfer faster and with better robustness against parameter fluctuations compared to previous methods.
method: The study employs Shortcuts to Adiabaticity (STA) techniques, combining Counter-diabatic (CD) driving with Time-Rescaling (TR) optimization to engineer the required Hamiltonian dynamics.
model_or_system: The system modeled is a chainwise-connected five-level quantum system. The analysis involves sequential reduction of the full Hamiltonian ($H_5$) down to effective two- and three-level descriptions ($	ilde{H}_2, 	ilde{H}_3$).
key_observables: Final population in the target state $|5\rangle$, transient populations of intermediate states (e.g., $|3\rangle$), and robustness against parameter fluctuations.
important_parameters: Rabi frequencies ($\Omega_i(t)$), detuning ($\delta$), time-rescaling parameters ($a$), and evolution time ($t_f$).
main_assumptions: The initial calculations rely on the Adiabatic Elimination (AE) principle due to computational difficulties in multi-level CD driving.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate population dynamics comparing different protocols ($	ext{M-STIRAP}$ vs. $	ext{M-STIRSAP}$ vs. $	ext{M-STIRSAP-opt}$) and show the dependence of final state populations on external parameters like detuning or time.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the need for STA in multi-level systems, developing protocols via Hamiltonian reduction ($H_5 ightarrow H_3 ightarrow H_2$), applying CD driving to create $	ext{M-STIRSAP}$, and finally optimizing this result using Time-Rescaling (TR) to yield the superior $	ext{M-STIRSAP-opt}$ protocol.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles advanced quantum control theory, which is central to designing coherent manipulation of atomic or superconducting qubits in AMO physics settings. The combination of CD driving and TR optimization represents state-of-the-art techniques for fast gate implementation.
